metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Afton, WY | Star Valley Owners
metaDescription: Own mineral rights under Star Valley ground near Afton, WY? Get a straight read on your Lincoln County interest from a Wyoming landman before you sign anything.
heroLead: Afton sits at the north end of Star Valley, and most of the mineral interests I run into up here trace back to homestead patents that split off the surface a generation or three ago.
intro: Star Valley never had the drilling density you saw over the ridge on the Moxa Arch or down at Fontenelle, but the Overthrust Belt runs under this whole corridor, and Lincoln County clerk records show plenty of old severed mineral deeds tied to Afton-area quarter sections. Most owners I talk to here inherited a fraction from a grandparent's ranch and have no idea what county or federal unit it actually sits in.

If you've got a royalty check that's dwindled to nothing, or a mineral deed you found in a probate file with no idea what it's worth, I'll pull the county records and tell you plainly what you're holding before you decide whether to sell.

sections.heading: Star Valley's thrust-belt geology
paragraphs: The Overthrust Belt stacks older rock on top of younger rock in long thrust sheets, and Star Valley sits on the western flank of that structural trend. Producing fields like Fontenelle and Whitney Canyon are miles east, but the same folded structures extend under Afton and Etna, which is why old operators leased broadly through here in the 1970s and 80s even where nothing was ever drilled.

A lot of what I find in Lincoln County deed books is exactly that: a lease that expired decades ago, followed by a severed mineral interest nobody ever touched again. The mineral estate stayed split from the surface even after the oil company walked away.

sections.heading: What your interest is worth
paragraphs: With no active wellbore nearby, an Afton mineral interest is priced on speculative held-for-future-development terms, not on current royalty income. That means the number depends heavily on proximity to the nearest producing unit, whether your tract has ever seen a lease, and how title reads in the courthouse. I quote against what similar undeveloped Lincoln County tracts have actually traded for recently, not a number pulled out of thin air.
If you do have a small royalty check coming from a unit further south toward the Moxa Arch, that changes the math entirely, and I'll walk you through both scenarios before you decide.

sections.heading: Clearing up inherited fractions
paragraphs: Star Valley ranch families have been splitting minerals among heirs since before anyone drilled a well here. By the third generation, a single quarter section might carry a dozen names, half of them out of state. I can usually work from the last recorded deed and a death certificate to confirm your share without you having to hire a title attorney first.

faqs.question: Is anyone actually drilling near Afton right now?
faqs.answer: Not directly under the town. Overthrust Belt activity has stayed concentrated east toward Fontenelle and Whitney Canyon for years, but Lincoln County holds old leasehold history across most of the valley, and interest can still trade on that basis.

faqs.question: I have a mineral deed with no legal description I understand. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send me a photo or copy and I'll match it to the section, township, and range in the Lincoln County records myself.

faqs.question: Do I need to sell my surface too?
faqs.answer: No. Mineral and surface are separate estates here, same as most of Wyoming. Selling the minerals doesn't touch your ranch or house.

faqs.question: What if my interest has never produced anything?
faqs.answer: That's common in Star Valley. It still has value as an undeveloped position, priced lower than a producing interest, and I'll give you a straight range for it.
